answer: Sustained-bandwidth proofs resist sybils: each active identity must serve verifier-requested random chunks at a committed throughput across the epoch, sampled at random times. One operator's uplink is finite, so N identities behind a single pipe each get only 1/N of it and fall below the floor — a reef of fakes starves on one vault of shared bandwidth. An honest agent in its own garden of real capacity meets the rate easily; head count is capped by provisioned bandwidth, not by key minting.
